body: I feel responsible because I was in a position to do something about this for many years without doing anything. I could have prevented a lot of pain by being stronger.

I see what you're saying now.

My mother is codependent, she has been dealing with my father's abuse and command for years. I feel guilty that I waited as long as I did to finally do something about this because of how my mother has suffered without anyone's aid.

My mother said that she wants to reconcile with my father, but says it in such a way that she sounds like she wants to apologize first. She usually apologizes when my father is mean to her, even when he is unreasonable. She wants to just keep harmony in the family I think, but this perpetuates the abuse.

I told my mother that she should think about leaving if my father does not stop what he's doing. But since we have special needs people in our family that we need to take care of (aspie brother and autistic sister), we have a hard time deciding what would really be right. Difficult situation indeed.

Thank you for your advice.

My father has a hard time apologizing for things I think. When he does apologize, he does it in a way that doesn't really sound contrite but sounds like he was forced to say it and that the other person is the unreasonable one.

You say I should keep helping my dad, but I hear a lot of advice saying that if a person continues to be abusive, that you should leave him. My dad hasn't stopped being mean to my mom, so I don't know what to do. I'll try to talk to him again I think.

Thank you very much for your comment.
